semin-durr:1-1.t: His saying: {الأعلى}: it may be genitive as an adjective of «ربِّك», and accusative as an adjective of «اسم». However, this rules out «الذي» being an adjective of «ربِّك»; rather it must be made an adjective of «اسم», or be cut off (maqṭūʿ), so as not to require separation between the adjective and the qualified noun by the adjective of another; for the construction would become like your saying «جاءني غلامُ هندٍ العاقلُ الحسنةِ» ("there came to me the servant of Hind, the intelligent, the beautiful (fem.)"), in which «العاقل» separates «هند» from its adjective. The discussion of annexing the name to the named has already been given.

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {ثُمَّ لاَ يَمُوتُ}: «ثم» is for the gap between ranks in severity.

semin-durr:16-16.t: His saying: {بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ}: Abū ʿAmr read it with the third person, and the rest with the second person; both are clear.

semin-durr:17-17.t: His saying: {وأبقى}: i.e. than this world.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {لَفِي الصحف}: Abū ʿAmr, in the transmission of al-Aʿmash and Hārūn, read it with sukūn on the ḥāʾ in both places, and this too is clear.

semin-durr:19-19.t:
His saying: {إِبْرَاهِيمَ}: the majority read it with an alif after the rāʾ and a yāʾ after the hāʾ; Abū Rajāʾ read it without them, the hāʾ with fatḥa or with kasra, so two readings are reported from him. Abū Mūsā and Ibn al-Zubayr read it with two alifs, and likewise throughout the Qur'an; Mālik ibn Dīnār read it with an alif after the rāʾ only, the hāʾ having fatḥa; and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Abī Bakr read «وإبْرَاهيم» without the alif and with kasra on the hāʾ. Ibn Khālawayh said: "«إبْراهُم» has also been reported," meaning with an alif and ḍamma on the hāʾ. The discussion of this noble name and its dialect forms has already been given in full in al-Baqara.
[Translator's note: in the source, the closing quotation mark after Ibn Khālawayh's statement is missing.]

semin-durr:3-3.t: His saying: {قَدَّرَ}: al-Kisāʾī read it with a light dāl; the rest read it with a doubled dāl. The two readings were given earlier in al-Mursalāt.

semin-durr:5-5.t:
His saying: {غُثَآءً}: either a second object or a ḥāl. al-Ghuthāʾ, with doubled thāʾ or light, the latter being the eloquent form, / is what the torrent deposits at the sides of the valley of plants and the like. Imruʾ al-Qays said:
4549 - كأنَّ ذُرا رأسِ المُجَيْمِرِ غُدوةً ... من السَّيْلِ والغُثَّاء فَلْكَةُ مِغْزَلِ
(As if the heights of the summit of al-Mujaymir at morning, with the torrent and its debris, were the whorl of a spindle.)
al-Farrāʾ transmitted it as «والأَغْثاء» in the plural; there is something unusual in it, in that he pluralised fuʿāl as afʿāl.
His saying: {أحوى}: there are two views on it, the clearer being that it is an adjective of «غُثاء». The second: that it is a ḥāl from «المَرْعَى». Abū l-Baqāʾ said: "He fronted part of the relative clause." I (al-Samīn) say: he means that the original is «أخرجَ المرعى أَحْوى فجعله غثاءً» ("He brought forth the pasture dark green, then made it debris"), but this is not called fronting part of the ṣila. al-Aḥwā is afʿal from al-ḥuwwa, which is a blackness tending toward greenness. Dhū l-Rumma said:
4550 - لَمْياءُ في شَفَتَيْها حَوَّةٌ لَعَسٌ ... وفي اللِّثاتِ وفي أَنْيابِها شَنَبُ
(Lamyāʾ, with a dark-red tinge on her lips, and on her gums and her teeth a cool brightness.)
You have already seen that some grammarians took this verse as evidence for the existence of badal al-ghalaṭ (substitute of mistake). It is also said: greenness with blackness upon it. al-Aḥwā is also the gazelle, because on its back are two lines. He said:
4551 - وفي الحَيِّ أَحْوَى يَنْفُضُ المَرْدَ شادِنٌ ... مُظاهِرُ سِمْطَيْ لُؤْلُؤٍ وزَبَرْجَدِ
(And in the tribe is a dark-lipped fawn, shaking the arāk-berries, wearing two strands, of pearl and of peridot.)
One says «رجلٌ أَحْوَى» and «امرأةٌ حَوَّاء», and the plural of both is «حُوٌّ», like «أحمر» and «حمراءُ» and «حُمْر».

semin-durr:6-6.t: {فَلاَ تنسى}: it is said to be a negation: the Exalted informed that His Prophet, peace be upon him, will not forget. It is also said to be a prohibition, with the alif being a lengthening; something like this was given earlier in Yūsuf and Ṭāhā. Makkī denied that it could be a prohibition because one is not forbidden what is not within his choice. This is not necessary, for the meaning is a prohibition against engaging in the causes of forgetting, and this is common.

semin-durr:7-7.t:
His saying: {إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ الله}: there are several views on it. One: that it is a complete exception (mufarragh), i.e. "except what Allah wills to make you forget, for you will forget it"; what is meant is the lifting of its recitation. In the hadith: "He used to wake up having forgotten verses," on the basis of His saying {مَا نَنسَخْ مِنْ آيَةٍ أَوْ نُنسِهَا} [البقرة: 106]. It is also said that the meaning of that is fewness and rarity, as it was reported that "he, peace be upon him, omitted a verse in his prayer; Ubayy supposed that it had been abrogated and asked him, and he said: 'I forgot it.'" al-Zamakhsharī said: "The aim is to negate forgetting altogether, as a man says to his companion: 'You are my partner in what I own, except what Allah wills,' not intending to except anything; and it is among the uses of fewness in the sense of negation." End of quotation. al-Farrāʾ and Makkī preceded him to this view. al-Farrāʾ and a group with him said: "This exception is a ṣila (filler) in speech following the practice of Allah the Exalted in exception; and there is no [thing] allowed to be excepted." The Shaykh said: "This ought not to occur in the speech of Allah the Exalted nor in any eloquent speech; likewise the view that «لا» is a prohibition and the alif a separator." End of quotation. What the Shaykh said was not intended by the one who called it a ṣila, i.e. purely redundant, but rather the meaning he mentioned, namely emphasis in negating forgetting or forbidding it.
Makkī said: "It is also said: the meaning of that is 'except what Allah wills', and Allah does not will that he forget anything of it, so it is like His saying in Hūd in both places: {خالِدِيْنَ فيها ما دامَتِ السماواتُ والأرضُ إلاَّ ما شاء ربُّك}, and He, exalted be His mention, did not leave out anything of the eternity because of the precedence of His will for their eternity." It is also said: it is an exception from His saying {فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَآءً أحوى}; Makkī related this. This ought not to be permitted at all.
His saying: {وَمَا يخفى}: «ما» is a noun (ismiyya). It cannot be maṣdariyya, lest the verb be left without an agent. Were it not for that, the maṣdariyya would be better, so that an interpreted maṣdar could be conjoined to a similar explicit one.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {وَنُيَسِّرُكَ}: conjoined to «سَنُقْرِئُك», so it comes within the scope of the relief (tanfīs, the future particle); and the sentence between them is parenthetical.

semin-durr:9-9.t:
His saying: {إِن نَّفَعَتِ}: «إنْ» is conditional. There is in it a sense of regarding their taking heed as remote. From this:
4552 - لقد أَسْمَعْتَ لو نادَيْتَ حَيَّاً ... ولكنْ لا حياةَ لمَنْ تُنادي
(You would have made yourself heard had you called one alive; but there is no life in the one you call.)
It is also said: «إنْ» means «إذْ», as in His saying {وَأَنْتُمُ الأَعْلَوْنَ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ} [آل عمران: 139]. It is also said: it means «قد»; Ibn Khālawayh mentioned it, and it is very remote. It is also said: something is omitted after it, the implied form being: "whether the reminder benefits or does not benefit"; al-Farrāʾ said this, and al-Naḥḥās, al-Jurjānī and al-Zahrāwī.
